title: Which cloud migration tool fits you?

questions.hint: Cloud migration is four different jobs. Pick the one that is biggest for you.

options.label: Files or buckets
options.why: you are moving files and objects

options.label: Data I will keep syncing for analysis
options.why: you want an ongoing copy for analysis

options.label: AWS
options.why: the cloud providers' own tools here send data to their own cloud only

options.label: Azure
options.why: the AWS and Google tools here send data to their own cloud only

options.label: Google Cloud
options.why: the cloud providers' own tools here send data to their own cloud only

options.label: A warehouse or lake, on any cloud
options.why: Google DMS lists Google Cloud databases only, with no lake or warehouse

questions.q: Is this a one-time cutover or an ongoing copy?

options.label: It should keep running
options.why: you want a copy that keeps running

questions.q: If the data goes to a warehouse or lake, who runs the pipeline?
questions.hint: Skip this one if you are not moving analytics data.

options.label: A vendor runs it
options.why: you want a vendor to run it

questions.q: Do you need a guaranteed delay on ongoing changes?

options.label: Yes, I need a guarantee
options.why: AWS says there are no SLAs for CDC latency

mgn.name: AWS Transform MGN
mgn.summary: AWS's own tool for rehosting physical, virtual and cloud servers on AWS, with continuous block-level replication.
mgn.bestWhen: AWS is the target and your servers run a supported operating system.
mgn.watchOut: Free for the first 90 days per server, then $0.042 per server per hour (checked Oct 2026). Support ends for Windows 2008, Windows 7 and CentOS 7 in late 2026.

azure.name: Azure Migrate or Azure DMS
azure.summary: Microsoft's tools for moving servers, SQL Server databases and web apps into Azure, with planning steps built in.
azure.bestWhen: You run a Windows and SQL Server estate heading to Azure.
azure.watchOut: Azure targets only. Web app moves cover ASP.NET on Windows, and Azure DMS (classic) for SQL Server was not supported after 15 March 2026.

gcpvm.name: Google Migrate to Virtual Machines
gcpvm.summary: Moves VMs from vSphere, AWS, Azure and Google Cloud VMware Engine to Compute Engine, with no service charge.
gcpvm.bestWhen: Your VMware, AWS or Azure virtual machines are going to Google Cloud.
gcpvm.watchOut: Physical servers are not listed as a source on the pages we read.

awsdms.name: AWS Database Migration Service
awsdms.summary: Runs a full load and then captures changes, from sources like Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL and MongoDB into AWS targets.
awsdms.bestWhen: A database is heading into AWS.
awsdms.watchOut: AWS says there are no SLAs for CDC latency, so changes have no guaranteed delay.

gcpdms.name: Google Database Migration Service
gcpdms.summary: One-time or continuous moves into Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, with no extra charge for native same-engine moves to Cloud SQL or AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.
gcpdms.bestWhen: The target is Cloud SQL or AlloyDB.
gcpdms.watchOut: Destinations are Google Cloud databases only, with no lake or warehouse.

files.name: AWS DataSync or Google Storage Transfer Service
files.summary: Bulk copies of file shares and buckets into AWS storage or Cloud Storage, with a worked price example on AWS's page.
files.bestWhen: You are moving file shares, archives or buckets.
files.watchOut: They copy files and objects only. DataSync names no database support, and Google's tool does not read table formats.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run, ongoing copy from databases, apps and files into warehouses and lakes, with 700 or more connectors.
fivetran.bestWhen: You want to feed a warehouse with little upkeep.
fivetran.watchOut: Not built for a one-time cutover, and Standard plan syncs run every 15 minutes at best (checked Oct 2026).

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A long connector list you can run yourself with the free Core edition, or use as a hosted Cloud edition.
airbyte.bestWhen: You want lots of connectors and can wait between syncs.
airbyte.watchOut: Syncs run on a schedule, and Cloud Standard syncs at most hourly (checked Oct 2026), so it is not a live cutover tool.
